questions.expected_answer: A. void Handler(object sender, string e)
questions.user_answer: Any method with signature void MethodName(object sender, EventArgs e) can subscribe to box.Changed
questions.followup_question: What is the correct method signature to subscribe to box.Changed for Box<string> and why?
questions.followup_answer:
For Box<string>, the event type is EventHandler<string>, so the correct handler is:
void OnChanged(object sender, string e)
questions.feedback: Answers are contradictory. The main answer is incorrect (EventHandler<T> is not EventHandler with EventArgs). The follow-up is correct: for Box<string> the handler must be void Handler(object sender, string e). Deducted points for initial misunderstanding/confusion.

questions.question: In C#, implement a simple Factory pattern: define an ILogger interface with a Log(string) method, two implementations ConsoleLogger (writes to Console) and NullLogger (does nothing), and a LoggerFactory with a static Create(string type) method that returns a ConsoleLogger when type == "Console" and a NullLogger otherwise. Then show sample usage creating a Console logger and logging "Hello".
questions.followup_question: Can you add the sample usage that creates a Console logger and logs "Hello" (e.g., var logger = LoggerFactory.Create("Console"); logger.Log("Hello");)?
questions.feedback: Excellent — provides ILogger, ConsoleLogger, NullLogger, and LoggerFactory.Create that returns ConsoleLogger for 'Console'; usage logs 'Hello'. Code compiles and behaves as expected.

You correctly attempted to address the event subscription by unsubscribing, but putting the unsubscribe in the finalizer is ineffective: because the Publisher holds a strong reference to the Subscriber via the event, the Subscriber will not become eligible for finalization, so the finalizer will never run. A proper fix is to unsubscribe deterministically (e.g., implement IDisposable and remove the handler in Dispose) or use a weak event pattern so Subscriber instances can be collected.

The candidate produced the correct fix — invoking the event with new ItemEventArgs<T>(item) using the null-conditional operator — and supplied corrected code that will compile. However, the initial list of 'bugs' contains incorrect or unnecessary items (ItemEventArgs already had a type parameter and Processor was already generic), which shows some confusion. A brief explanation that EventHandler<TEventArgs> requires an instance of the TEventArgs type would make the answer clearer.
